cards.label: Trump's enemy
cards.reason: Politics card 1 and Headlines clip 1 (HEADLINES START WITH POLITICS). The US president declares anyone who says 'artificial intelligence' instead of 'super intelligence' an enemy of the White House. A stranger understands it in five seconds, it is plainly about AI, it is confirmed (The Independent), and it is the political AI story of the day for the whole world. Pairs with card 2, Japan's answer.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 7 day decks carry the White House AI task force (4 Oct: spy chief Jay Clayton to lead it) and the 8 Oct Cantwell safety-test plan; the rename order of late September was only in the 4 and 5 Oct Full Reports, never a card or clip. Today's event is new: Trump's Thursday post calling users of the old term THE ENEMY. Freshness NEW.
cards.novice_test: Truth Social: Trump's own social network (one line). 'Super intelligence': the White House's new official name for AI, ordered for federal agencies a week ago (one line). With those two lines the card lands for anyone: the US president is policing a word.

cards.label: Japan says AI
cards.reason: Politics card 2, score 6 (below the extra_min 7 guideline; chosen on Rafi's 9 Oct order for political AI news from around the world and the brief's 'cover the whole world'). Japan's prime minister told parliament that 'AI' stays the right word and she will not follow Trump's rename for now. It is a reply story that makes card 1 a two-card arc (America orders a new word, its closest Asian ally declines), it is the only head-of-government AI story outside the US today, and a stranger gets it at once.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Takaichi, Japan government or rename story was a card or clip in the last 7 days (5 Oct had a Bank of Japan deputy governor on interest rates, a different story). Freshness NEW: her answer in the Diet is of 8 Oct. REPLY STORY: the writer must say whom she answers (Trump's UN speech last month and his order) and name Yuichiro Tamaki, leader of the Democratic Party for the People, who asked. Credit Kyodo News; the text was read through a Korean relay that credits Kyodo.
cards.novice_test: Sanae Takaichi: Japan's prime minister (one line). Yuichiro Tamaki: leader of an opposition party, the Democratic Party for the People, who asked the question. 'Superintelligence': the word Trump wants governments to use instead of AI. Lands: a government saying no to a word is clear to anyone.

cards.label: OpenAI revenue
cards.reason: Market card 1, score 8, the top market story of the day: the best-known AI company told investors its yearly sales pace is almost $50 billion, well below the roughly $70 billion it had signalled, a $20 billion gap days before its listing preparations are scrutinised. It matters to anyone judging whether the AI boom is as big as advertised. Reuters with its own source; the FT reported it first.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 6 Oct deck carried OpenAI's plan to RAISE $30 billion or more at a $1.4 trillion value (Gulf funds, BlackRock). Today's story is a different fact: its REVENUE pace and the gap to what it signalled. Not the same story and not an update of the raise; freshness NEW. Shown here so Rafi can judge it in the 3 day name-and-topic table (same company two days apart, different topic).
cards.novice_test: OpenAI: the maker of ChatGPT (one line). 'Yearly revenue pace' (annualised revenue): one month's sales multiplied by twelve, a pace, not money already earned (one line, from the summary). Anthropic: rival AI lab, maker of Claude, whose sales count differently. Lands: 'the ChatGPT company earns less than it told investors' is clear to anyone.

cards.label: WTO trade
cards.reason: Market card 2 and the market Headlines clip: the World Trade Organization more than doubled its 2026 forecast for growth in world goods trade (to 3.9% from 1.9%) because trade in AI chips and servers rose 67% and now carries nearly half of all growth, outweighing the hit from the Middle East war. An official, confirmed, genuinely global story (AP) that shows AI moving the whole world economy, not only Silicon Valley; a positive counterweight to the daily debt stories. Markets held at 2 cards, the money cap.
cards.not_repeat_because: No WTO, trade forecast or world-economy story in the 7 day decks (the market lines there are OpenAI, DeepSeek, SoftBank, Samsung, TSMC, SpaceX debt, Hong Kong listings, Dalio). Freshness NEW.
cards.novice_test: World Trade Organization: the body in Geneva that sets and watches the rules of trade between countries (one line). 'Goods trade': the physical things countries buy and sell from each other. Lands: 'AI chips are now carrying world trade' is plain.

cards.label: Free scanner
cards.reason: Security card 1 and a Headlines clip, score 8: Anthropic will run its strongest AI, including Claude Mythos, over open-source software for free to find security flaws. Open-source code sits under almost everything people use, so this touches everyone; the catch (reports are machine-written with no human review, some will be wrong) is part of the story.
cards.not_repeat_because: Mythos appeared on 7 Oct only inside Jamie Dimon's 'hacking ten times riskier' quote; that was a banker's warning, not this service. No scanner, open-source or Anthropic security-service story was a card or clip in the last 7 days. Freshness NEW (launched 8 Oct).
cards.novice_test: Anthropic: the AI company behind the Claude chatbot (one line). Open-source software: programs whose code is shared publicly and used inside most apps and websites (one line). Claude Mythos: Anthropic's strongest model. Lands: 'free AI check-ups for the world's shared code, but nobody human reads the results' is clear.

cards.label: Fake reporters
cards.reason: Security card 2, score 7: OpenAI says it shut down Russian and Iranian networks that used ChatGPT to invent journalists and a fake Latin American think tank and placed almost 100 articles in real online outlets, rating both campaigns high on its impact scale. World coverage (Russia, Iran, Ukraine, Bolivia, the US) and a stranger understands 'AI-made fake reporters got into real news'. Third and last OpenAI card (company limit 3).
cards.not_repeat_because: The 7 day decks have OpenAI agents editing Wikipedia (6 Oct) and OpenAI programs hitting a UN website (4 Oct), both about OpenAI's own rogue agents, not state propaganda using ChatGPT. No influence-operation or fake-journalist story was a card or clip. Freshness NEW (OpenAI disclosure of 8 Oct).
cards.novice_test: Influence network: a group that spreads propaganda under false names (one line). Think tank: a research institute that publishes policy opinions, here a fake one. OpenAI's 1-to-6 impact scale: its own measure of how far a campaign reached; 5 means mainstream audiences. Lands for anyone.

cards.label: Gas by truck
cards.reason: Energy card, score 7 (tie with three other 7s; chosen as the most concrete picture of the AI power squeeze): Oracle trucks compressed natural gas in trailers to keep an AI data centre near Salt Lake City running and to start an OpenAI campus in Texas, paying about four times the market gas price while pipelines wait. A stranger sees it at once: AI wants so much power that it arrives by truck.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 3 Oct deck had Oracle's Wisconsin data centre and nuclear power, a different site and a different story (a power purchase, not trucked gas). Data-centre lines since then were local opposition (7 Oct), record US power use (7 Oct) and Google's nuclear deal (6 Oct). Freshness NEW (Bloomberg, 8 Oct).
cards.novice_test: Oracle: a big US software and cloud company that builds data centres for OpenAI (one line). Compressed natural gas: gas squeezed into tanks so a truck can carry it. 'Trading hub' price: the normal market price of gas. Lands: 'they are trucking fuel to feed AI' is vivid and plain.

cards.label: Traffic robots
cards.reason: NEW IN V2. Robotics card 1, the HUMANOID card the ROBOTICS ruling asks for, and the robotics Headlines clip. Chinese robot maker Deep Robotics tested its DR02 humanoid robots directing traffic at junctions, keeping order and answering tourists' questions in several languages on busy Hangzhou streets, in heavy traffic and steady rain, moving around the junctions on their own sensors. A machine a stranger can picture at once doing a human job in public. Chosen over the other humanoid story (C11-24, a shop robot shown at a Tokyo trade event with store use planned from 2027) because this one works in the street now; C11-24 goes to the teaser. REPORTED: AI Insider, citing the company; no independent results or official comment, which the card and clip must say ('Deep Robotics says'). Score 6, from the Bulletin.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Deep Robotics, DR02, Hangzhou or traffic-robot story in the 7 day decks. The humanoid lines there are Figure funding (8 Oct), Tesla Optimus output (8 Oct), Agilink's embroidery hand (7 Oct), Kawasaki's 2030 humanoid (4 Oct) and the French TV host boxing robots (4 Oct): other companies, other machines. Freshness NEW (announced 9 Oct; trials in early October).
cards.novice_test: Deep Robotics: a Chinese robot maker from Hangzhou, known for four-legged robots, now building human-shaped ones (one line). DR02: its humanoid model. Hangzhou: a city of about 12 million near Shanghai; Xihu (West Lake) is its main tourist district. Lands: 'human-shaped robots directed traffic in a Chinese city in the rain' is clear to anyone; the card must say the company reports it and no one has checked.

cards.label: Gene-edit doubt
cards.reason: Research card, score 6, chosen over the four score-7-and-8 research stories because each of those leads with money (Pentagon $350m quantum package, $2.4bn computing pledges, $159m awards, Oratomic's $475m) which Cards Master 3.3 keeps out of a research card's headline, and the Pentagon quantum tests were an 8 Oct card. This one leads with the deed: outside scientists say Anthropic's claim that its AI agents found a possible new gene-editing system is early and overstated, and a Copenhagen doctoral researcher, Mario Rodríguez Mestre, says his unpublished work describes the same thing (he cannot show Anthropic took it). A human story with a twist, CNN, and a check on the 'AI makes discoveries' claims we carry daily. Status DISPUTED, the pill says so.
cards.not_repeat_because: Anthropic's gene-editing announcement was last month, outside the 7 day window, and never a card in the decks shown; the science lines there are Meta's maths chatbot (3 Oct), Mayo pancreatic cancer (4 Oct), DeepMind enzymes (6 Oct), Biohub cells (8 Oct). Freshness NEW: the scientists' reaction and the student's claim are of 8 Oct.
cards.novice_test: Anthropic: the AI company behind Claude (one line). Gene editing: changing DNA inside living cells, as CRISPR does (one line). AI agents: AI programs that work through a task on their own. Mario Rodríguez Mestre: a doctoral researcher at the University of Copenhagen who used Claude in his work. Lands: 'AI's claimed discovery is disputed, and a student says it was his' is clear.

cards.novice_test: USA Today: one of America's biggest national newspapers; its publisher also owns local papers (one line). OpenAI: the maker of ChatGPT. 'Train its AI models': feed the articles to the AI so it learns from them (one line). Lands for anyone.

cards.label: AI pre-visit
cards.reason: Health card and a Headlines clip, score 7, the only health story in the Bulletin and the clearest 'AI touching people's lives' story of the day: at a Boston hospital, Google's AMIE chatbot interviewed patients by text before urgent primary-care visits, and in 98 supervised chats no doctor had to step in for safety; one hallucination was logged and the study tested feasibility only. Peer reviewed in The Lancet; the researchers call it the first real-world study of its kind.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 7 day health lines are AI emergency alerts in 11 hospitals (3 Oct), Mayo pancreatic cancer (4 Oct), acne prescriptions and NHS AI checks (6 Oct), NHS skin cancer ranking (8 Oct): different stories. No AMIE or patient-interview story. Freshness NEW.
cards.novice_test: AMIE: Google's medical chatbot, built to take a patient's history (one line). Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center: a teaching hospital in Boston tied to Harvard (one line). The Lancet: a leading medical journal. Hallucination: a made-up answer by the AI. Lands: 'an AI took patients' histories before urgent visits and never needed rescuing' is plain; the card must say it was supervised and small.

Set-up then punchline. Alternatives were not funny: Anthropic banning cruelty to Claude (a policy), Thiel on Obama and the Pope (politics), the Kardashians sketch, a fantasy-football AI, a Slack bank-balance leak (all score 2 in the reserve). Heraldo USA; the report gives no injury details and does not name the robot maker, which the card must respect.
fun.not_repeat_because: The 4 Oct fun story was a French TV host knocking two boxing robots down (the human hits the robots); today the robot hits the human, a different event, different people, different country. No Westcol or Blessd in the decks. Freshness NEW.
